title: RTI Reveals: In SIR, Purging of ‘Ineligibles’ from the Voter Lists Might be a Bogey
shows: The author asked the Election Commission and the Home Ministry under the RTI Act on 10 August 2026 whether electors the Commission found to be non-citizens had been referred to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, as the Supreme Court ordered in May 2026 to be done within four weeks. The Commission replied after 50 days that it held none of the information, and the Home Ministry passed the application on the same day to the Legislative Department, which sent it back to the Commission, so no reply named the competent authority or gave a number of cases referred.
quote: On August 10, this author filed two RTI applications to ascertain compliance with the Supreme Court’s directions. The first was submitted to the ECI and the second, to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs
the Commission shall refer such cases within 4 weeks to the Competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955, for adjudication of their citizenship.

After 50 days (against the statutory deadline of 30 days), its Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) replied (see Image 3 below) saying that it did not have any of the information sought in the RTI application.

MHA transferred the RTI application to the legislative department of the Union law ministry on the same day it was filed. Two days later, the legislative department sent the RTI application to the ECI physically
The MHA itself does not seem to know who is the authority competent to adjudicate such matters.
note: Byline line on the page: 'Venkatesh Nayak is Director, Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative, New Delhi.'
